Decided 2026-08-20: one Rust version. rust-version raised to 1.97.1 to equal .mise.toml's pin, the msrv CI job and the check-msrv mise task deleted, and a renovate.json rule added keeping the rust pin out of automerge so raising the floor stays reviewed. Recorded as ADR-0025.

Measurement is what settled it, and it went further than the proposal assumed. With --ignore-rust-version, oakum compiles on 1.85 through 1.90 — six minor versions below the declared 1.91 floor. Below that the binding constraint is the toml DEV-dependency family (toml, serde_spanned, toml_datetime, toml_parser all declare rust-version = 1.85), which no consumer of the binary links, so the shipping floor was lower still. Nothing in oakum required 1.91.

Also established: the declaration is self-enforcing, which is why it drifted unnoticed — at 1.88 and 1.90 cargo refuses with 'requires rustc 1.91' before compiling anything, so the number could only be falsified by opting out on purpose. And the counter this issue asked the ADR to answer turned out sharper than stated: renovate.json sets automerge true with minor and patch grouped, so a rust pin bump would have landed unreviewed. Renovate is configured here but has never opened a PR, so it was prospective; the new rule closes it either way.
